title: Minimum Cost to Move Chips to The Same Position
statement:
There are `n` chips on a number line; chip `i` sits at `position[i]` (several chips may share a spot). You may move any chip as often as you like, one step at a time:

- shifting a chip by exactly 2 in either direction is free;
- shifting a chip by exactly 1 in either direction costs 1.

Return the smallest total cost that gathers every chip onto one common position.
notes:
## Intuition

A free jump of 2 never changes whether a chip is on an odd or an even spot, so every chip can slide for free to any spot of its own parity. Only crossing between odd and even costs anything, and one paid step of 1 is enough to cross. So pick a meeting spot of one parity: every chip of the other parity pays exactly 1, and the rest pay nothing. The cheapest choice moves the smaller group.

## Approach

1. Count the chips on odd spots (`odd`) and on even spots (`even`).
2. Gather everything on a spot whose parity matches the larger group; each chip of the smaller group pays 1.
3. Return `Math.min(odd, even)`.

## Example 1, step by step

`position = [1, 2, 3]`.

- `p = 1` is odd: `odd = 1`.
- `p = 2` is even: `even = 1`.
- `p = 3` is odd: `odd = 2`.

Meet at an odd spot such as 1: the chip at 3 jumps there for free and the chip at 2 pays 1. The answer is `min(2, 1) = 1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over the chips.
- Space: O(1): two counters.

## Pitfalls

- The actual distances do not matter; `[1, 1000000000]` still costs only 1.
- Simulating moves or trying every target between the smallest and largest position is far too slow when positions reach 10^9.
- Chips sharing a spot each count separately: `[2, 2, 2, 3, 3]` costs 2, not 1.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `odd` | number of chips on odd positions |
| `even` | number of chips on even positions |
| `p` | the current chip's position |

narration.2: Count of chips that sit on odd positions.
narration.3: Count of chips that sit on even positions.
narration.5: Look at every chip once; only its parity matters.
narration.6: Is this chip on an even spot?
narration.7: Yes: it joins the even group.
narration.9: No: it joins the odd group.
narration.12: Meet on the larger group's parity, so only the smaller group pays 1 each.
